# Tabs
Switches between sibling views inside one screen, without navigating.

**When to use** — two to five peer views of the same subject; a segmented choice between named options.
**When not to** — steps in a sequence (use a flow), or navigation between routes (NavBar).

## Variants
`underline` content sections · `pills` compact, on subtle surfaces · `enclosed` boxed.
Figma names these `line` `pill` `segmented`; the code has not been renamed yet and `segmented` is a restyle, not just a rename (see `state/discrepancies.json`).

## Composition
`TabsRoot` + `TabsList` + `TabsTrigger` + `TabsPanel`, or the `Tabs` convenience wrapper with an `items` array.

## Do
- Keep the panel content the same shape across tabs so the page doesn't jump.
- Let arrow keys move between triggers — the component handles it; don't override.
- Use a Badge inside a trigger for counts.

## Don't
- Don't build a segmented control out of raw buttons — use `pills`.
- Don't hide a required form field behind an unselected tab.

```tsx
<TabsRoot value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}>
  <TabsList aria-label="Theme"><TabsTrigger value="light">Light</TabsTrigger></TabsList>
</TabsRoot>
```
